steps.prompt: Which story would you keep reading?
steps.a: Ella went to the shop, bought some milk, and went home. It was a nice day.
steps.b: Ella had five minutes to get the milk home before her mum found out she'd used the last of it on a science experiment.
steps.reveal: The second one has a conflict: something stands in Ella's way, and there's a clock ticking. Without conflict, nothing happens. With it, you need to know how it ends.

cards.title: Conflict
cards.body: Conflict is the problem or struggle at the heart of a story: something the character wants, and something in the way. No conflict, no story.

cards.title: Six kinds of conflict
cards.body: Person vs person (a rival or bully), person vs self (a fear or hard choice), person vs nature (a storm, a wild animal), person vs society (an unfair rule), person vs technology (a machine gone wrong) and person vs supernatural (ghosts, magic, the impossible).

cards.title: Same character, different conflicts
cards.text: Leo wants to win the swimming race. A rival cheats (person vs person). Leo panics in deep water (person vs self). A storm closes the outdoor pool (person vs nature).
cards.note: Changing the conflict changes the whole story, even with the same character and the same want.

cards.title: Find the conflict
cards.prompt: Tap the two words that show what stands in Maya's way.
cards.text: Maya wanted to reach the summit before dark, but the blizzard grew stronger and the trail vanished under fresh snow.

prompts: Which conflict did you choose, and why?
What does your character want, and what is standing in the way?
